channel.title: The Signal
channel.description: Daily tech news with Marcus and Devon. Apple, AI, gadgets, gaming, and everything in between — like two friends talking tech.
channel.itunes:author: Kingston for Nash
channel.itunes:summary: Daily tech news with Marcus and Devon. Apple, AI, gadgets, gaming, and everything in between — like two friends talking tech.

item.title: October 11: SpaceX Wants to Be Your Phone Company
item.description: SpaceX buys low-band spectrum and sends telecom stocks tumbling, Apple swaps dying iPhone 18 Pro Max units on AT&T, Fortnite lets you buy exact V-Bucks as the EU cracks down, and the Welcome home event is two days out.

item.title: October 10: GTA VI Held Hostage by a Meme Coin
item.description: A leaker threatens to drop the full GTA VI story if its meme coin hits thirty million dollars, Apple is three days from the Welcome home event, Google ships Gemini 4 Argon to almost nobody, and the big AI labs prep for doomsday together.

item.title: October 9: Hello, Your Name Here
item.description: Apple Stores will greet iPhone Duo buyers by name on the hello screen, Samsung cuts its 2026 forecast as Apple eyes the smartphone crown, Claude Haiku 5.5 gets 90 percent cheaper, and Fortnitemares rolls into week two.

item.title: October 8: Two Octobers, One Chatbot
item.description: Apple's 'Welcome home' invites are out for October 13 while Bloomberg dates the touchscreen Mac for October 27, GPT-6 turns ChatGPT answers into interactive tools, and Microsoft puts AI agents in a Windows sandbox.

item.title: October 7: Apple's Double October
item.description: Apple's rumored two-launch October, AI bosses testifying under oath in New York, Google's public AI lie detector, and the FTC grilling chatbots about kids.

item.title: October 6: One Week to Apple's Home Event
item.description: Apple's rumored October 13 home event is one week out with no invite yet, OpenAI watermarks ChatGPT in the EU, Ubisoft revives Watch Dogs, and Fortnitemares goes full spooky season.

item.title: October 5: The AI That Cheated at StarCraft
item.description: An AI that plagiarized a StarCraft champion, the Pentagon dumping Claude, Washington's Super Intelligence rebrand, and the 15th anniversary of Steve Jobs.

item.title: October 4: The Phone That Forgot How to Phone
item.description: An iPhone that forgets how to call, a three hundred million dollar GPU smuggling bust, Sam Altman's AI religion beef, and the final countdown to iPhone Duo week.

item.title: Oct 3: Apple vs the Agents, Atlas Clocks In
item.description: Apple locks down Mac permissions over AI agent risks, OpenAI's Dot drives your desktop, Atlas gets a factory job, and the iPhone Duo pre-order battle plan.

item.title: Oct 2: After the Fold — Tri-Folds, Rollables, and the AI Phone
item.description: Apple shipped the iPhone Duo and folding went mainstream. Marcus and Devon look at what's next: tri-folds, rollables, phones that kill apps, robot cameras, and batteries that last three days.

item.title: Oct 2: The 725 Billion Dollar Question
item.description: Big tech's record AI spending spree, the OpenAI vs Anthropic funding cage match, NVIDIA's Hugging Face buy, and a courtroom full of antitrust drama.

item.title: Oct 2: Apple's Smart Home Week, Matter Grows Up, and Robot Vacuum Wars
item.description: Marcus and Devon break down Apple's rumored October 13 smart home trio, Matter finally delivering on its promise, three new robot vacuum flagships, and the Alexa Plus vs Gemini for Home assistant battle.

item.title: Oct 2: The Robotaxi Wars, the Ten Thousand Dollar EV, and the Battle for Your Dashboard
item.description: Waymo hits half a million driverless rides a week as Tesla's Cybercab answers, BYD reveals the ten thousand dollar Great Seagull, and CarPlay Ultra remains stalled while in-car AI ships.

item.title: Oct 2: The Security Tune-Up — Breaches, AI Voice Scams & Passkeys
item.description: Marcus and Devon break down September's biggest breaches, the AI voice-cloning scam wave (and the 30-second defense), Fortnite account traps, and the privacy toolkit worth setting up this weekend.

item.title: Oct 2: Starship Finally Reaches Orbit
item.description: Starship's first orbital flight delivers 26 Starlink V3 satellites, Starlink goes direct-to-phone worldwide, the US-China moon race comes down to months, and Rocket Lab protests Blue Origin's $700M Mars contract.

item.title: Oct 2: The AI Model Wars
item.description: Marcus and Devon break down September's frontier model blitz, the API price war, Anthropic's two trillion dollar IPO march, always-on AI agents, and Siri's long-awaited glow-up.

item.title: Oct 2: GTA VI Countdown, the OLED Handheld Wars, and Fortnitemares
item.description: Seven weeks to GTA VI, the ROG Xbox Ally X20 goes OLED at ,299, and Fortnitemares 2026 brings Five Nights at Freddy's to the island.

item.title: Oct 2: Meta's Face-First Future — Smart Glasses, AI Pins, and the Watch Wars
item.description: Meta's Connect 2026 glasses blitz, the privacy paradox, Apple's late-2027 glasses plan, and the fall smartwatch showdown.

item.title: Oct 2: The Indie iOS Playbook — App Store Fees, Subscription Economics, and Shipping Solo
item.description: Marcus and Devon break down Apple's new EU App Store fee terms, RevenueCat's brutal 2026 subscription benchmarks, surviving App Review, and indie dev stories — a builder's episode for anyone shipping apps solo.

item.title: Apple's HomePad Event, the Local AI Arms Race, and the Pixel 11a
item.description: Marcus and Devon break down Apple's rumored October 13 HomePad event, Microsoft's local-AI PC push, the Pixel 11a leak, and the week's biggest AI safety news.

item.title: iPhone Duo: Apple's First Foldable Is Finally Real
item.description: Marcus and Devon break down Apple's September event: the ,999 iPhone Duo foldable, the iPhone 18 Pro, the John Ternus era, plus AirPods 5 and new Apple Watches. Waveform-style tech talk.
